state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.text: Why do you think you forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive in this case? Can you think of a different way to approach expanding the brackets that might help you keep track of the signs more effectively?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I just got confused with the signs when I was expanding. Maybe if I write out each step more carefully, like showing the negative signs clearly, it would help me not to miss them. Can you show me how to do that step by step?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of a specific strategy that might help you keep track of the signs more effectively as you expand the brackets? Perhaps considering the distributive property or using a color-coding system for positive and negative terms could be helpful. What do you think?
